Let $\mathbb F$ be $\mathbb R$ or $\mathbb C$, let $m,n\in\mathbb{N}$ and let
$A=(a_{ij})\in M_{m\times n}(\mathbb F)$. The **Frobenius norm** of $A$ is

$$\lVert A\rVert_F\;:=\;\Bigl(\,\sum_{i<m}\sum_{j<n}|a_{ij}|^{2}\Bigr)^{1/2},$$

where $|\cdot|$ is the absolute value on $\mathbb R$
([[def-abs-value]]) for $\mathbb F=\mathbb R$ and the modulus on $\mathbb C$
([[def-complex-conjugate-real-imaginary-part-and-modulus]]) for
$\mathbb F=\mathbb C$, and the outer power is the nonnegative real square root.

**The displayed quantity is a norm.** Regard $A$ as the element of the
coordinate space $\mathbb F^{mn}$ whose $j+in$-th entry is $a_{ij}$. The
standard coordinate inner product of [[prop-standard-coordinate-inner-products]]
satisfies $\langle A,A\rangle=\sum_{i,j}a_{ij}\overline{a_{ij}}$, which equals
$\sum_{i,j}|a_{ij}|^{2}$ because $z\overline z=|z|^{2}$
([[lem-complex-conjugation-and-modulus-laws]]). Thus $\lVert A\rVert_F$ is
exactly the inner-product norm of [[def-inner-product-norm]] evaluated at $A$,
and the three norm axioms hold for $\lVert\cdot\rVert_F$ because they hold for
every inner-product norm. For real matrices the same sum is
$\sum_{i,j}a_{ij}^{2}$, since $|x|^{2}=x^{2}$ for real $x$ by the two cases of
[[def-abs-value]].

The Frobenius norm is the Euclidean norm of the full entry list, not the
largest factor by which the matrix stretches a single vector. It can coincide
with an induced $2$-norm in one-row or one-column cases, but in general it is a
different matrix norm from the induced operator norms used on this page. Its
relation to the spectral norm, its unitary invariance and its singular-value
formula are
[[thm-spectral-and-frobenius-norms-are-unitarily-invariant-with-singular-value-formulas-and-rank-comparison]].

derivations.claim: Put $M(t)=e^{tA}$. For finite matrices $P,R$, $\|PR\|_F^2=\sum_j\|PR e_j\|_2^2\le\|P\|_2^2\sum_j\|R e_j\|_2^2=\|P\|_2^2\|R\|_F^2$ by the operator-norm definition and [F4]. The entry formula in [F4] gives $\|R^*\|_F=\|R\|_F$. The SVD in [F5] gives the same positive singular values for $P$ and $P^*$; [F6] therefore gives $\|P^*\|_2=\|P\|_2$. Applying the left-multiplication estimate to adjoints yields $\|RP\|_F\le\|R\|_F\|P\|_2$. Applying these inequalities successively gives $\|M(t)QM(t)^*\|_F\le\|M(t)\|_2^2\|Q\|_F$.
For $X_T=\int_0^T M(t)QM(t)^*\,dt$, [F2] and the product rule give $\frac{d}{dt}(M(t)QM(t)^*)=AM(t)QM(t)^*+M(t)QM(t)^*A^*$. Integrating this identity yields $AX_T+X_TA^*=M(T)QM(T)^*-Q$.

By [F1], the right side in step 1.1 is bounded by a finite sum of polynomial multiples of $e^{-2\alpha t}$. Each such term is integrable on $[0,\infty)$ by repeated integration by parts. Every entry of the integrand is therefore absolutely integrable; define $X$ by the finitely many scalar improper entry integrals. The entrywise tails tend to zero, so $X_T\to X$ in Frobenius norm and the matrix integral converges absolutely in that norm. The integrand is self-adjoint because $Q=Q^*$.
By [F1], $M(T)QM(T)^*\to0$ as $T\to\infty$, and by step 2.1, $X_T\to X$. Taking limits in step 1.2 gives $AX+XA^*=-Q$.

Suppose $Q\succeq0$. By [F3], $Q^{1/2}$ exists and is self-adjoint, so $Q=(Q^{1/2})^*Q^{1/2}$. Hence for every $v$, $v^*Xv=\int_0^\infty\|Q^{1/2}e^{tA^*}v\|_2^2\,dt\ge0$. Thus $X\succeq0$. If $Q\succ0$ and $v\ne0$, the integrand at $t=0$ is $v^*Qv>0$ and is continuous, so it stays positive on an interval of positive length; therefore $v^*Xv>0$ and $X\succ0$.

If $Y$ is another solution, $H=Y-X$ satisfies $AH+HA^*=0$. The derivative of $M(t)HM(t)^*$ is therefore zero by [F2], so it is constant and equals $H$ at $t=0$. By [F1] it tends to zero as $t\to\infty$, hence $H=0$ and the solution is unique.

For $Q\succeq0$ and nonzero $v$, the continuous integrand in step 3.2 has integral zero exactly when it vanishes for all $t\ge0$: if it were positive at one time, continuity would make its integral over a neighboring interval positive. It vanishes at time $t$ exactly when $e^{tA^*}v\in\ker Q^{1/2}$. Hence $v^*Xv>0$ for every nonzero $v$ exactly when no nonzero trajectory remains in that kernel for all $t\ge0$.

Let $F\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$, $m,n\ge1$, $A\in F^{m\times m}$ and $B\in F^{n\times n}$. Spectra of real matrices are taken over $\mathbb C$. The map $\mathcal S_{A,B}$ of [[def-sylvester-operator-and-separation-number]] is invertible if and only if

$$
\sigma(A)\cap(-\sigma(B))=\varnothing.
$$

Equivalently, for every $C\in F^{m\times n}$, the equation $AX+XB=C$ has a unique solution if and only if this spectral condition holds. The same condition is equivalent to $\operatorname{sep}(A,-B)>0$.
citations.use_explanation: [[thm-sylvester-unique-solvability-spectral-separation]]: [[thm-sylvester-unique-solvability-spectral-separation]]: A Sylvester operator is invertible exactly when the coefficient spectra are disjoint, and its separation is positive exactly in that case.

citations.quote:
Let $X$ be the unique solution of $AX+XB=C$, and let $\widehat X\in F^{m\times n}$ be any approximation. Define its equation residual by $R=C-(A\widehat X+\widehat X B)$. If $\operatorname{sep}(A,-B)>0$, then

$$
\|X-\widehat X\|_F\le\frac{\|R\|_F}{\operatorname{sep}(A,-B)}.
$$
citations.use_explanation: [[thm-sylvester-residual-to-forward-error-bound]]: [[thm-sylvester-residual-to-forward-error-bound]]: For a unique Sylvester solution, the Frobenius forward error is at most the Frobenius equation residual divided by separation.

citations.quote:
Let $A\in F^{n\times n}$ be Hurwitz and let $Q=Q^*\in F^{n\times n}$. Then the improper matrix integral

$$
X=\int_0^\infty e^{tA}Qe^{tA^*}\,dt
$$

converges and is the unique solution of $AX+XA^*+Q=0$. If $Q\succeq0$, then $X\succeq0$. If $Q\succ0$, then $X\succ0$. For $Q\succeq0$, $X\succ0$ if and only if there is no nonzero $v$ for which $e^{tA^*}v\in\ker Q^{1/2}$ for every $t\ge0$.
citations.use_explanation: [[thm-continuous-lyapunov-integral-and-positivity]]: [[thm-continuous-lyapunov-integral-and-positivity]]: For Hurwitz $A$, the integral $X$ exists uniquely and satisfies $AX+XA^*+BB^*=0$.

Let $\mathbb F$ be $\mathbb R$ or $\mathbb C$, let $A\in M_{m\times n}(\mathbb F)$, and
let $\sigma_1\ge\sigma_2\ge\cdots\ge\sigma_r>0$ be the positive singular values of
$A$, where $r=\operatorname{rank}A$; write $\sigma_1=0$ when $r=0$.

1. **Spectral formula.** $\lVert A\rVert_2=\sigma_1$, where $\lVert\cdot\rVert_2$ is
   the operator norm of [[def-operator-norm-on-a-finite-dimensional-inner-product-space]].
2. **Frobenius formula.** $\lVert A\rVert_F=\bigl(\sigma_1^{2}+\cdots+\sigma_r^{2}\bigr)^{1/2}$.
3. **Unitary invariance.** For every unitary $U\in M_m(\mathbb F)$ and
   $V\in M_n(\mathbb F)$ (over $\mathbb F=\mathbb R$: orthogonal matrices),
   $$\lVert UAV\rVert_2=\lVert A\rVert_2,\qquad \lVert UAV\rVert_F=\lVert A\rVert_F.$$
4. **Sharp rank comparison.**
   $$\lVert A\rVert_2\;\le\;\lVert A\rVert_F\;\le\;\sqrt{r}\,\lVert A\rVert_2.$$
   The lower inequality is an equality exactly when $r\le 1$; the upper
   inequality is an equality exactly when $\sigma_1=\cdots=\sigma_r$, that is,
   when all nonzero singular values coincide. In particular
   $\lVert A\rVert_F\le\sqrt{\min(m,n)}\,\lVert A\rVert_2$.
citations.use_explanation: [[thm-spectral-and-frobenius-norms-are-unitarily-invariant-with-singular-value-formulas-and-rank-comparison]]: [[thm-spectral-and-frobenius-norms-are-unitarily-invariant-with-singular-value-formulas-and-rank-comparison]]: The Frobenius norm is unitarily invariant and its square is the sum of squared singular values.

Let $T:V\to W$ be a linear map between finite-dimensional inner product spaces. In orthonormal bases $\mathcal E=(e_j)$ of $V$ and $\mathcal F=(f_i)$ of $W$,

$$[T^*]_{\mathcal E\leftarrow\mathcal F}=\overline{[T]_{\mathcal F\leftarrow\mathcal E}}^{\mathsf T}.$$

Over $\mathbb R$ this is the transpose. The statement includes zero-sized bases.

For every $n\ge1$, every commutative ring $R$, and every $A\in M_n(R)$,
$$\det(A^{\mathsf T})=\det(A).$$

Complex conjugation is a real-field automorphism satisfying
$$\overline{z+w}=\overline z+\overline w,\qquad \overline{zw}=\overline z\,\overline w,\qquad \overline{\overline z}=z.$$
For every $z,w\in\mathbb C$,
$$z\overline z=|z|^2,\qquad |z|\ge0,\qquad |z|=0\Longleftrightarrow z=0,$$
$$|zw|=|z||w|,\qquad |z+w|\le |z|+|w|.$$

Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $n\ge1$, and let $A=(a_{ij})\in M_n(R)$. Its **determinant** is
$$\det(A):=\sum_{\sigma\in S_n}\operatorname{sgn}(\sigma)\prod_{i<n}a_{\sigma(i),i}.$$
The sum is finite because $S_n$ has $n!$ elements. The product is taken in $R$, so the signs $1$ and $-1$ act through the ring identities. The formula uses columns indexed by $i<n$ and rows indexed by $\sigma(i)$.

When $A$ is real, $|\det A|$ means the ordinary real absolute value of its real determinant. It is not alternate notation for the determinant itself.

derivations.claim: From [F1], $R_j=\left(I-2\operatorname{Re}(p_j)(A+p_jI)^{-1}\right)R_{j-1}=(A-\overline{p_j}I)(A+p_jI)^{-1}R_{j-1}$, since $-2\operatorname{Re}(p_j)=-(p_j+\overline{p_j})$. All factors are rational functions of $A$ and commute, so iterating gives $R_j=\rho_j(A)B$.

In the standard orthonormal basis, [F7] represents $A^*$ by $\overline A^{\mathsf T}$. For $z\in\mathbb C$, [F8] and [F10] give $\det(zI-A^*)=\det((zI-\overline A)^{\mathsf T})=\det(zI-\overline A)$, and [F9] applied to the Leibniz formula gives $\det(zI-\overline A)=\overline{\det(\overline z I-A)}$. Hence $\sigma(A^*)=\overline{\sigma(A)}$, so both $A$ and $A^*$ have spectrum in the open left half-plane; therefore $\sigma(A)\cap(-\sigma(A^*))=\varnothing$. By [F3], $\operatorname{sep}(A,-A^*)>0$. Subtracting the equation for $X_j$ in [F2] from the exact equation in [F5] gives $\mathcal S_{A,A^*}(X-X_j)=-R_jR_j^*$.
Applying the operator bound in [A1] to each column of $B$ and summing squared column norms gives $\|R_j\|_F\le\eta_j\|B\|_F$.

Apply [F4] to step 1.2. If $R_j=U\Sigma V^*$ is an SVD, then $R_jR_j^*=U\Sigma^2U^*$, so unitary invariance and [F6] give $\|R_jR_j^*\|_F^2=\sum_i s_i(R_j)^4\le(\sum_i s_i(R_j)^2)^2=\|R_j\|_F^4$. Therefore $\|X-X_j\|_F\le\|R_jR_j^*\|_F/\operatorname{sep}(A,-A^*)\le\eta_j^2\|B\|_F^2/\operatorname{sep}(A,-A^*)$. Since $\eta_j\to0$ and the separation is positive, the right side tends to zero.

Input a real or complex square matrix $A\in\mathbb F^{n\times n}$ with $n\ge1$, a finite nonnegative deflation tolerance $\tau$, a nonnegative integer sweep budget $N$, a positive integer stagnation period $h$, finite tables of finite exceptional shifts, optional exact rational/dyadic encodings of its stored real values, and optionally a terminating exact evaluator of [[def-exact-real-2x2-discriminant-sign-predicate]]. A formation `breakdown` is propagated with the operation index and partial factors. Every scalar operation is evaluated in the operationwise model of [[def-operationwise-real-complex-floating-point-model-with-sqrt-and-fma]]. Any invalid, overflow, or underflow operation returns range-failure with the operation index and partial factors.

For each stored reflector with active indices $S=(s_1,\ldots,s_m)$, vector $v\in\mathbb F^m$, and real computed coefficient $\widehat\tau$, the real or complex formation routine first performs the stated finite left application. Then perform the right application in this fixed order: for each matrix row $i=1,\ldots,n$, compute $d_i=\operatorname{fl}(\sum_{a=1}^m H^L_{i,s_a}v_a)$ by left-to-right rounded products and additions; for $a=1,\ldots,m$, compute $c_a=\operatorname{fl}(\widehat\tau\overline{v_a})$, $g_{ia}=\operatorname{fl}(d_ic_a)$, and $H^R_{i,s_a}=\operatorname{fl}(H^L_{i,s_a}-g_{ia})$. Each complex product uses the six real operations of the arithmetic model. The exact factor appended to $Q$ is $P(v)=I-2vv^*/(v^*v)$; the computed right update uses $\widehat\tau$ as displayed and is not asserted equal to multiplication by $P(v)$. For a matrix-target column, the formation routine's explicit zero writes are retained. In the initial polynomial-vector step there is no matrix-target column: use the entire active row panel for the left update and then apply the right update to the active columns. Record deflation writes separately, including a pure deflation with no following reflector as an identity-transform stage; a local error certificate must account for all other rounding and target-column writes.

1. Reduce $A$ to upper Hessenberg form with Householder similarities. For $k=1,\ldots,\max(n-2,0)$ in increasing order, use active indices $S=\{k+1,\ldots,n\}$, target $x=H_{S,k}$, and trailing left panel $B=H_{S,\{k+1,\ldots,n\}}$ with columns in increasing order. In the real branch use [[alg-scaled-householder-reflector-formation-and-application]] for the finite left application and overwrite; in the complex branch use [[alg-complex-scaled-householder-reflector-step]]. Complete each similarity by the right application above on columns $S$. If the resulting matrix fails the exact upper-Hessenberg zero-pattern check, return bulge-chase-invariant-failure with the partial factors. Store the exact unitary reflector factors as a product representation $Q_0$.
2. At each sweep, test every active first-subdiagonal entry by
   $$|h_{i,i-1}|\le\tau\bigl(|h_{i-1,i-1}|+|h_{i,i}|\bigr).$$
   For a complex entry $z=a+ib$, evaluate $|z|$ by $s=\max(|a|,|b|)$ and $s\sqrt{(a/s)^2+(b/s)^2}$ when $z\ne0$, with divisions, squares, sum, square root and final scaling rounded in the stated order; use $|0|=0$. Return range-failure if this evaluation fails. Compute the diagonal-magnitude sum first, then multiply by $\tau$ in the operationwise model; compare the resulting finite values exactly. When the test holds, set that entry to zero, record its original value as a deflation perturbation, and split the active block. The equality case deflates. Do not use the Hermitian-tridiagonal Wilkinson shift rule for a general Hessenberg matrix.
3. Check for the target Schur block structure after initialization and after each sweep. A complex active block of size at least two uses a single shift, normally its bottom-right entry. A real active block of size at least two uses the real quadratic $p(z)=z^2-sz+t$ with trailing block $\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\c&d\end{pmatrix}$; compute $s=\operatorname{fl}(a+d)$ and $t=\operatorname{fl}(\operatorname{fl}(ad)-\operatorname{fl}(bc))$ in that order, returning range-failure if an operation fails. Maintain a counter for each active block, reset it after any deflation in that block, and after $h$ consecutive sweeps without deflation consume that block's next declared exceptional shift or real quadratic. If the required table entry is absent, return stagnation-exhausted.
4. Apply the corresponding implicit bulge chase from [[alg-exact-francis-hessenberg-qr-step]]. For the initial single-shift vector compute $x_1=\operatorname{fl}(h_{11}-\mu)$ and $x_i=h_{i1}$ for $i>1$. For the initial real double-shift vector, compute $u=He_1$, then $w=Hu$ by left-to-right rounded matrix-vector products, then $x=\operatorname{fl}(\operatorname{fl}(w-su)+te_1)$ componentwise. Compute only the first $r+1$ components from the Hessenberg support pattern; on range failure return the operation index and partial factors. For a chase at column $j$, use active indices $S=I_j$, target $x=H_{S,j}$, and trailing left panel $B=H_{S,\{j+1,\ldots,n\}}$ with columns in increasing order. Call the real or complex formation routine, write the target tail zeros exactly, complete the two-sided update by the right-kernel order above on columns $S$, and append the exact reflector representation to $Q$. In the initial polynomial-vector step there is no matrix-target column; use the full active row panel for the left update and then apply the right update to its active columns. If the exact routine or its finite-precision realization returns bulge-chase-invariant-failure, return that status with the partial matrix and factors. Use [[lem-two-sided-scaled-householder-similarity-error]] to store the proved two-sided coefficient $\alpha_{m_j}=a_{m_j}+b_{m_j}+a_{m_j}b_{m_j}$, with $a$ the target-overwrite coefficient or separate-block coefficient as actually used and $b$ the right separate-block coefficient. This gives $\|E_j\|_F\le\alpha_{m_j}\|\widehat H_{j-1}\|_F$ when its $m_ju<1$ and range hypotheses hold. Apply the same certificate to every Hessenberg-initialization similarity. If any step lacks that certificate, retain the residual diagnostic and set the backward-error-certificate status to inconclusive.
5. Stop with Schur-computed when every complex block has size one, or every real block has size one or is a $2\times2$ block with negative characteristic-polynomial discriminant. Use the supplied evaluator, or the finite integer recipe in [[lem-exact-rational-two-by-two-discriminant-sign]] when exact rational/dyadic encodings are available, for each real block's $\operatorname{discSign}$ as defined in [[def-exact-real-2x2-discriminant-sign-predicate]]. If no exact sign is available, return schur-type-undecided and do not claim Schur-computed. If the target check fails when the sweep count reaches $N$, return budget-exhausted; in particular, with $N=0$ return Schur-computed only when the initialized matrix already has the target block structure. Return the partial matrix and factors on every failure or nonconvergence status.

Let $\widehat T$ be the final returned matrix. The output includes the product representation $Q$, residual matrix $R=Q^*AQ-\widehat T$ and its Frobenius norm as diagnostics, the exact orthogonality bound $0$ for that reflector product, the recorded deflation entries, and either the accumulated backward-error bound when all local certificates exist or certificate status inconclusive. Bound expressions and any claimed upper bounds are evaluated exactly or with rigorous outward allowances; uncorrected rounded residual norms are diagnostics only. A rounded dense matrix formed from $Q$ has its own orthogonality residual and is not asserted exactly unitary. The residual diagnostic does not itself give a forward eigenvalue bound. The procedure asserts no unconditional convergence of any shift schedule.

Let $\mathbb F$ be $\mathbb R$ or $\mathbb C$, let $n\ge0$ and $A\in\mathbb F^{n\times n}$, and let $Q^*$ denote transpose over $\mathbb R$ and conjugate transpose over $\mathbb C$. A **complex Schur pair** for $A$ is a pair $(Q,T)$ with $Q^*Q=I$ and $A=QTQ^*$, where $T$ is upper triangular.

For real $A$, a **real Schur pair** is a pair $(Q,T)$ with $Q^TQ=I$ and $A=QTQ^T$, where $T$ is block upper triangular and every diagonal block is either a real $1\times1$ block or a real $2\times2$ block with negative characteristic-polynomial discriminant. Such a $2\times2$ block has one nonreal conjugate eigenvalue pair. The definition does not assert that a finite shift strategy reaches such a pair.

For $B=\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\c&d\end{pmatrix}\in\mathbb R^{2\times2}$, its characteristic-polynomial discriminant means the exact real number $\Delta(B)=(a+d)^2-4(ad-bc)$. “Negative discriminant” means the exact comparison $\Delta(B)<0$.

For $F\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$, $A\in F^{m\times m}$, $B\in F^{n\times n}$ with $m,n\ge1$, define the Sylvester operator $\mathcal S_{A,B}:F^{m\times n}\to F^{m\times n}$ by

$$\mathcal S_{A,B}(X)=AX+XB.$$

Equip $F^{m\times n}$ with the Frobenius norm of [[def-frobenius-matrix-norm]]. The column-vectorization isometry of [[lem-sylvester-vectorization-isometry-and-kronecker-identity]] identifies this norm with the Euclidean norm on $F^{mn}$. Define

$$\operatorname{sep}(A,-B):=\sigma_{\min}(\mathcal S_{A,B})=\min_{\|X\|_F=1}\|AX+XB\|_F.$$

Here $\sigma_{\min}$ denotes the smallest singular value of the finite-dimensional linear map under these inner products. The finite-dimensional singular value decomposition [[thm-singular-value-decomposition]] ensures this minimum is well-defined. The argument $-B$ is part of the conventional label: the operator being measured is $X\mapsto AX+XB$.

Let $F\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$, $q\ge1$, and $M\in F^{q\times q}$. Define

$$\delta(M)=\begin{cases}0,&\|M\|_F=0,\\[2pt]\dfrac{|\det M|}{\|M\|_F^{q-1}},&\|M\|_F>0.\end{cases}$$

With the empty product convention when $q=1$, $0\le\delta(M)\le\sigma_{\min}(M)$.

Let $F$ be a field, $q\ge1$, and $M\in F^{q\times q}$. Let $\operatorname{adj}(M)$ be the adjugate defined by the cofactors of [[def-matrix-minors-cofactors-and-adjugate]]. Then

$$
M\operatorname{adj}(M)=\det(M)I_q.
$$

Consequently, when $\det(M)\ne0$, $M^{-1}=\operatorname{adj}(M)/\det(M)$; when $\det(M)=0$, $M$ is singular.

For a real matrix $B=\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\c&d\end{pmatrix}$, define its characteristic-polynomial discriminant by $\Delta(B)=(a+d)^2-4(ad-bc)$. Define $\operatorname{discSign}(B)$ to be $-1$, $0$, or $1$ according as the exact real number $\Delta(B)$ is negative, zero, or positive. This is an exact mathematical predicate on the stored real entries, not an operation in the operationwise floating-point model. A computed procedure may report a sign only when its control predicate establishes this exact value; otherwise it reports undecided.

Suppose the stored entries of $B=\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\c&d\end{pmatrix}$ have supplied exact rational encodings $a=p_a/q_a$, $b=p_b/q_b$, $c=p_c/q_c$, $d=p_d/q_d$, with integer numerators and positive integer denominators. Put $Q=q_aq_bq_cq_d$ and $A=p_a(Q/q_a)$, $B_0=p_b(Q/q_b)$, $C_0=p_c(Q/q_c)$, $D=p_d(Q/q_d)$. Compute the integer
$$Z=(A-D)^2+4B_0C_0.$$
Its integer sign is exactly [[def-exact-real-2x2-discriminant-sign-predicate]] and is found after finitely many exact integer operations. Finite binary floating values with their signed-integer/power-of-two encodings are a special case. This evaluator does not assume arbitrary stored real numbers have rational encodings. If an exact encoding or another terminating exact sign evaluator is unavailable, retain `schur-type-undecided`.

The local transforms, certificate checks and block substitution use exact scalar arithmetic and comparisons. The delegated Schur calls retain their specified rounded arithmetic, admissible input representations, range conditions and statuses; their returned factors remain candidates until the exact checks below succeed.

The default real-block sign controller is the fixed exact real-arithmetic expression tree $s=(a-d)^2+4bc$, followed by its sign comparisons, for [[def-exact-real-2x2-discriminant-sign-predicate]]. This uses five exact arithmetic operations and at most two sign comparisons in the declared exact local arithmetic model. For rational/dyadic encoded stored values, [[lem-exact-rational-two-by-two-discriminant-sign]] gives the finite exact integer realization; a fixed-format decoder, when used, is included in the control cost. These exact controller operations are separate from the rounded Schur matrix updates. No bit-complexity bound for integer/rational arithmetic is claimed.

Choose either bounded-controller mode, the default, or arbitrary-terminating-controller mode. In bounded mode supply a nonnegative integer per-call budget $K$. Custom sign or decoding routines are finite instruction programs over exact scalar real/integer arithmetic, comparisons, register operations and branches; no opaque callback is a unit instruction. The interpreter charges one unit per executed instruction, including decoding, the built-in tree and any custom-result verification within the same per-call $K$ budget; it checks instruction/operation validity when encountered and returns undecided on exhaustion or invalid execution. An undecided sign is propagated as the Schur type-undecided status and then outer `schur-failure`. The fixed built-in sign tree or integer recipe has a fixed finite instruction count independent of matrix dimension. Any custom reported sign must agree with the built-in exact discriminant tree before acceptance. In arbitrary-terminating mode custom programs must terminate on every supplied input; record their total executed controller work as $C_{\rm aux}$. This richer mode retains finite termination but has the additional work in its cost bound. In the cubic-cost branch $K$ and representation-control instruction costs are fixed independently of matrix dimension. Programs are executed by instruction lookup without an up-front scan of unused code.

1. Run [[alg-finite-budget-francis-schur-reduction]] on $A$ and $B$ with their supplied controls and budgets. If either call does not return `Schur-computed`, return `schur-failure` with the underlying status.

2. Treat the returned factors as candidates and verify the exact certificates. In the complex branch check $U^*U=I$, $A=UTU^*$, and upper triangularity of $T$; in the real branch check $U^TU=I$, $A=UTU^T$, and the real block upper-triangular form of [[def-real-and-complex-schur-forms]]. $$
F_{ij}=D_{ij}-\sum_{k>i}T_{ik}Y_{kj}-\sum_{\ell<j}Y_{i\ell}S_{\ell j}.
$$

The terms on the right have already been computed in this traversal order. Define $\Phi_{ij}(Z)=T_{ii}Z+ZS_{jj}$ and its matrix representation $M_{ij}=I_{s_j}\otimes T_{ii}+S_{jj}^T\otimes I_{r_i}$ on column-vectorized blocks, where $r_i,s_j\in\{1,2\}$ are the block sizes. Let $q=r_is_j\le4$ and compute $\delta(M_{ij})$ from [[lem-small-block-determinant-separation-lower-bound]]. If $\det(M_{ij})=0$, return `singular-pivot`; if $\det(M_{ij})\ne0$ and $\delta(M_{ij})\le\tau$, return `pivot-separation-failure` because the requested pivot bound is not certified. Otherwise use the cofactor adjugate formula of [[lem-adjugate-inverse-formula-over-a-field]] to set $\operatorname{vec}(Y_{ij})=\operatorname{adj}(M_{ij})\operatorname{vec}(F_{ij})/\det(M_{ij})$ and store $Y_{ij}$. 4. After all blocks are solved, return `success` and $X=UYV^*$, together with the exact residual $C-(AX+XB)$. No computed Schur candidate is accepted as an exact factorization unless step 2 verifies its defining equalities.

For $F\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$, $A\in F^{m\times m}$, $B\in F^{n\times n}$ with $m,n\ge1$, define the Sylvester operator $\mathcal S_{A,B}:F^{m\times n}\to F^{m\times n}$ by

$$\mathcal S_{A,B}(X)=AX+XB.$$

Equip $F^{m\times n}$ with the Frobenius norm of [[def-frobenius-matrix-norm]]. The column-vectorization isometry of [[lem-sylvester-vectorization-isometry-and-kronecker-identity]] identifies this norm with the Euclidean norm on $F^{mn}$. Define

$$\operatorname{sep}(A,-B):=\sigma_{\min}(\mathcal S_{A,B})=\min_{\|X\|_F=1}\|AX+XB\|_F.$$

Here $\sigma_{\min}$ denotes the smallest singular value of the finite-dimensional linear map under these inner products. The finite-dimensional singular value decomposition [[thm-singular-value-decomposition]] ensures this minimum is well-defined. The argument $-B$ is part of the conventional label: the operator being measured is $X\mapsto AX+XB$.

Let $F\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$, $m,n\ge1$, $A\in F^{m\times m}$ and $B\in F^{n\times n}$. Spectra of real matrices are taken over $\mathbb C$. The map $\mathcal S_{A,B}$ of [[def-sylvester-operator-and-separation-number]] is invertible if and only if

$$
\sigma(A)\cap(-\sigma(B))=\varnothing.
$$

Equivalently, for every $C\in F^{m\times n}$, the equation $AX+XB=C$ has a unique solution if and only if this spectral condition holds. The same condition is equivalent to $\operatorname{sep}(A,-B)>0$.

derivations.claim: By [F1], $A=UTU^*$, $B=VSV^*$, and $D=U^*CV$ hold exactly. Multiplying $AX+XB$ on the left by $U^*$ and on the right by $V$ gives $TY+YS$.

In the $(i,j)$ block, $TY+YS$ equals $T_{ii}Y_{ij}+Y_{ij}S_{jj}+\sum_{k>i}T_{ik}Y_{kj}+\sum_{\ell<j}Y_{i\ell}S_{\ell j}$. The successful local solve from [F1] makes this block equal $D_{ij}$, so every block of $TY+YS$ equals the corresponding block of $D$.
Therefore $TY+YS=D=U^*CV$. Multiplying by $U$ on the left and $V^*$ on the right yields $A(UYV^*)+(UYV^*)B=C$. By [F2], this is $\mathcal S_{A,B}(X)=C$ for the returned $X=UYV^*$.
Under the stated spectral-disjointness condition, [F3] gives uniqueness for this right-hand side; hence the returned exact solution is the unique one.

Proof steps 2.1 and 3.1 establish the exact block equation and AX+XB=C even when C is zero. Under the separate spectral-disjointness hypothesis, step 4.1 also gives uniqueness for this homogeneous right-hand side.
For one-by-one inputs, proof step 2.1 consists of one local scalar block equation with both previous-block sums empty; step 3.1 transports that exact equality back through the verified factors.

The Statement is conditional on a successful certified return. Proof step 1.1 uses the verified exact Schur identities, and step 4.1 imposes spectral disjointness only for its additional uniqueness conclusion; no failed candidate is promoted to a solution.

Let $F\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$, $m,n\ge1$, $A\in F^{m\times m}$, $B\in F^{n\times n}$ and $C\in F^{m\times n}$. Inputs also include a pivot threshold $\tau\ge0$, Schur controls for each matrix, a fixed constant $c_0>0$, and finite sweep budgets $N_A\le c_0m$, $N_B\le c_0n$. The delegated Schur calls retain their specified rounded arithmetic, admissible input representations, range conditions and statuses; their returned factors remain candidates until the exact checks below succeed.

The default real-block sign controller is the fixed exact real-arithmetic expression tree $s=(a-d)^2+4bc$, followed by its sign comparisons, for [[def-exact-real-2x2-discriminant-sign-predicate]]. For rational/dyadic encoded stored values, [[lem-exact-rational-two-by-two-discriminant-sign]] gives the finite exact integer realization; a fixed-format decoder, when used, is included in the control cost. These exact controller operations are separate from the rounded Schur matrix updates. No bit-complexity bound for integer/rational arithmetic is claimed.

Choose either bounded-controller mode, the default, or arbitrary-terminating-controller mode. In bounded mode supply a nonnegative integer per-call budget $K$. Custom sign or decoding routines are finite instruction programs over exact scalar real/integer arithmetic, comparisons, register operations and branches; no opaque callback is a unit instruction. The interpreter charges one unit per executed instruction, including decoding, the built-in tree and any custom-result verification within the same per-call $K$ budget; it checks instruction/operation validity when encountered and returns undecided on exhaustion or invalid execution. An undecided sign is propagated as the Schur type-undecided status and then outer `schur-failure`. The fixed built-in sign tree or integer recipe has a fixed finite instruction count independent of matrix dimension. Any custom reported sign must agree with the built-in exact discriminant tree before acceptance. In arbitrary-terminating mode custom programs must terminate on every supplied input; record their total executed controller work as $C_{\rm aux}$. This richer mode retains finite termination but has the additional work in its cost bound. In the cubic-cost branch $K$ and representation-control instruction costs are fixed independently of matrix dimension. Programs are executed by instruction lookup without an up-front scan of unused code.

1. Run [[alg-finite-budget-francis-schur-reduction]] on $A$ and $B$ with their supplied controls and budgets. If either call does not return `Schur-computed`, return `schur-failure` with the underlying status.

2. Treat the returned factors as candidates and verify the exact certificates. In the complex branch check $U^*U=I$, $A=UTU^*$, and upper triangularity of $T$; in the real branch check $U^TU=I$, $A=UTU^T$, and the real block upper-triangular form of [[def-real-and-complex-schur-forms]]. 3. Set $D=U^*CV$. Use the column-vectorization and Kronecker convention of [[lem-sylvester-vectorization-isometry-and-kronecker-identity]]. Partition $T$ into diagonal blocks $T_{ii}$ and $S$ into diagonal blocks $S_{jj}$ as in the exact real or complex Schur form. Traverse $j$ from left to right and, for each $j$, traverse $i$ from bottom to top. Form

$$

$$

The terms on the right have already been computed in this traversal order. Define $\Phi_{ij}(Z)=T_{ii}Z+ZS_{jj}$ and its matrix representation $M_{ij}=I_{s_j}\otimes T_{ii}+S_{jj}^T\otimes I_{r_i}$ on column-vectorized blocks, where $r_i,s_j\in\{1,2\}$ are the block sizes. Let $q=r_is_j\le4$ and compute $\delta(M_{ij})$ from [[lem-small-block-determinant-separation-lower-bound]]. If $\det(M_{ij})=0$, return `singular-pivot`; if $\det(M_{ij})\ne0$ and $\delta(M_{ij})\le\tau$, return `pivot-separation-failure` because the requested pivot bound is not certified. Otherwise use the cofactor adjugate formula of [[lem-adjugate-inverse-formula-over-a-field]] to set $\operatorname{vec}(Y_{ij})=\operatorname{adj}(M_{ij})\operatorname{vec}(F_{ij})/\det(M_{ij})$ and store $Y_{ij}$. The local dimension is at most four in the real block case and one in the complex triangular case.

4. After all blocks are solved, return `success` and $X=UYV^*$, together with the exact residual $C-(AX+XB)$. No computed Schur candidate is accepted as an exact factorization unless step 2 verifies its defining equalities.

Input a real or complex square matrix $A\in\mathbb F^{n\times n}$ with $n\ge1$, a finite nonnegative deflation tolerance $\tau$, a nonnegative integer sweep budget $N$, a positive integer stagnation period $h$, a finite family of exceptional-shift tables $T_{a,b}$ indexed by original contiguous index intervals $[a,b]\subseteq[1,n]$ with $a<b$, optional exact rational/dyadic encodings of its stored real values, optionally a terminating exact evaluator of [[def-exact-real-2x2-discriminant-sign-predicate]], and optionally a terminating outward evaluator for nonnegative expressions and Frobenius norms. The outward evaluator's `upadd`, `upmul`, and `upsqrt` calls return finite nonnegative represented upper bounds for the exact sum, product, and square root, while `upnormF(X)` returns a finite represented upper bound for $\|X\|_F$; any call may instead return `unavailable`. In the declared scalar-cost model, each `upadd`, `upmul`, and `upsqrt` call has unit cost and `upnormF(X)` makes one pass over the entries of $X$ with a fixed number of such calls per real component. The evaluator acts only on certificate bookkeeping. A formation `breakdown` is propagated with the operation index and partial factors. Every scalar operation in the main procedure is evaluated in the operationwise model of [[def-operationwise-real-complex-floating-point-model-with-sqrt-and-fma]]. Any invalid, overflow, or underflow operation in the main procedure returns range-failure with the operation index and partial factors.

Each complex table entry is a finite represented scalar $\mu\in\mathbb C$; each real table entry is a pair of finite represented real coefficients $(s,t)$ for $z^2-sz+t$. Each table is an ordered finite list, possibly empty; an omitted interval has the empty list. These descriptors use the field of $A$. Tables support direct indexed lookup by interval and cursor; unused entries are not scanned. All interval-state updates use a single ordered pass over the current partition. Counters and table indices are exact integers. Maintain state $(c_{a,b},q_{a,b})$, initially $(0,0)$, for each current maximal diagonal interval separated by exact zero subdiagonals: $c$ counts completed ordinary block sweeps since the last reset and $q$ counts exceptional descriptors already consumed. After a split, discard the parent state and initialize every new child interval to $(0,0)$, using its own table. An unchanged interval retains its state. Completed one-by-one blocks, and real two-by-two blocks with verified negative discriminant, require no shift.

Start with $H=A$ and the empty factor product $Q=I$. Set the completed global sweep count to $k=0$ after initialization. Before attempting any sweep, and after every completed sweep, perform steps 2 and 5, in that order. If neither returns, snapshot the remaining active intervals in increasing left endpoint, and perform steps 3 and 4 once for each snapshotted interval in that order. No deflation scan or repartition occurs during this pass. After all its intervals finish, increment $k$ by one and repeat the scan and stopping test. All intervals in a pass use their current diagonal block when reached; previously applied similarities on disjoint blocks do not reschedule a block.

Before every real or complex formation in steps 1 and 4, test the target vector componentwise for exact zero, including an external initial polynomial vector. If it is zero, mark the stage `identity`, copy all affected matrix entries unchanged, skip formation and both left and right updates, append the embedded identity $P_j=I$ to the product representation, and record $E_j=0$ and arithmetic coefficient $\alpha_j=\bar\alpha_j=0$. Do not evaluate $P(v)$ or a stored-vector norm in this branch. For a matrix target its column is already zero, so its target zero writes change nothing; for an external vector no matrix column is overwritten. Continue with the invariant checks, sweep counters and stopping tests specified below. Record and process every deflation write separately exactly as specified below; this branch does not discard a deflation perturbation. These identity instructions take precedence over the formation/update instructions in steps 1 and 4.

For each nonidentity stored reflector with active indices $S=(s_1,\ldots,s_m)$, nonzero vector $v\in\mathbb F^m$, and real computed coefficient $\widehat\tau$, the real or complex formation routine first performs the stated finite left application. Then perform the right application in this fixed order: for each matrix row $i=1,\ldots,n$, compute $d_i=\operatorname{fl}(\sum_{a=1}^m H^L_{i,s_a}v_a)$ by left-to-right rounded products and additions; for $a=1,\ldots,m$, compute $c_a=\operatorname{fl}(\widehat\tau\overline{v_a})$, $g_{ia}=\operatorname{fl}(d_ic_a)$, and $H^R_{i,s_a}=\operatorname{fl}(H^L_{i,s_a}-g_{ia})$. Each complex product uses the six real operations of the arithmetic model. The exact factor appended to $Q$ is $P(v)=I-2vv^*/(v^*v)$; the computed right update uses $\widehat\tau$ as displayed and is not asserted equal to multiplication by $P(v)$. For a matrix-target column, the formation routine's explicit zero writes are retained. In the initial polynomial-vector step there is no matrix-target column: use the entire active row panel for the left update and then apply the right update to the active columns. Record deflation writes separately, including a pure deflation with no following reflector as an identity-transform stage; a local error certificate must account for all other rounding and target-column writes.

1. Reduce $A$ to upper Hessenberg form with Householder similarities. For $k=1,\ldots,\max(n-2,0)$ in increasing order, use active indices $S=\{k+1,\ldots,n\}$, target $x=H_{S,k}$, and trailing left panel $B=H_{S,\{k+1,\ldots,n\}}$ with columns in increasing order. In the real branch use [[alg-scaled-householder-reflector-formation-and-application]] for the finite left application and overwrite; in the complex branch use [[alg-complex-scaled-householder-reflector-step]]. Complete each similarity by the right application above on columns $S$. If the resulting matrix fails the exact upper-Hessenberg zero-pattern check, return bulge-chase-invariant-failure with the partial factors. Store the exact unitary reflector factors as a product representation $Q_0$.
2. In increasing global row index $i=2,\ldots,n$, test each nonzero first-subdiagonal entry by
   $$|h_{i,i-1}|\le\tau\bigl(|h_{i-1,i-1}|+|h_{i,i}|\bigr).$$
   For a complex entry $z=a+ib$, evaluate $|z|$ by $s=\max(|a|,|b|)$ and $s\sqrt{(a/s)^2+(b/s)^2}$ when $z\ne0$, with divisions, squares, sum, square root and final scaling rounded in the stated order; use $|0|=0$. Return range-failure if this evaluation fails. Compute the diagonal-magnitude sum first, then multiply by $\tau$ in the operationwise model; compare the resulting finite values exactly. When the test holds, set that entry to zero and record its original value as a deflation perturbation. After the scan, form the maximal intervals separated by exact zero subdiagonals and update interval states by the rule above. The equality case deflates. Do not use the Hermitian-tridiagonal Wilkinson shift rule for a general Hessenberg matrix.
3. For the current snapshotted interval $[a,b]$, let $L=H_{a:b,a:b}$ and $\ell=b-a+1$. If $c_{a,b}=h$, read entry $q_{a,b}+1$ of $T_{a,b}$. If absent, return stagnation-exhausted before this block's chase. Otherwise consume it by incrementing $q_{a,b}$ once and use its complex scalar shift or real coefficient pair. After this exceptional block sweep completes, set $c_{a,b}=0$. If $c_{a,b}<h$, use the ordinary shift: in the complex branch $\mu=L_{\ell,\ell}$; in the real branch, for the trailing block $\begin{pmatrix}a'&b'\\c'&d'\end{pmatrix}$, compute $s=\operatorname{fl}(a'+d')$ then $t=\operatorname{fl}(\operatorname{fl}(a'd')-\operatorname{fl}(b'c'))$ in that order. Return range-failure on a failed operation. After this ordinary block sweep completes, increment $c_{a,b}$ by one. A split at the next scan resets each new child as specified above; unchanged intervals retain these updated states.
4. On the diagonal block $L$ selected in step 3, apply the index pattern of [[alg-exact-francis-hessenberg-qr-step]], with its dimension $\ell$ and local indices $1,\ldots,\ell$. In the vector formulas in this step, $H$ means that current diagonal block. Translate every local index $i$ to global index $a+i-1$; embed each factor in the full $n\times n$ identity. The left panel extends through global column $n$, and the right application runs through all global rows, so upper off-diagonal blocks are updated as well. For the initial single-shift vector compute $x_1=\operatorname{fl}(h_{11}-\mu)$ and $x_i=h_{i1}$ for $i>1$. For the initial real double-shift vector, compute $u=He_1$, then $w=Hu$ by left-to-right rounded matrix-vector products, then $x=\operatorname{fl}(\operatorname{fl}(w-su)+te_1)$ componentwise. Compute only the first $r+1$ components from the Hessenberg support pattern; on range failure return the operation index and partial factors. For a chase at local column $j$, use the globally translated active indices $S=I_j$, the corresponding global target column $a+j-1$, and the trailing left panel through global columns $a+j,\ldots,n$ in increasing order. Call the real or complex formation routine, write the target tail zeros exactly, complete the two-sided update by the right-kernel order above on columns $S$, and append the exact reflector representation to $Q$. In the initial polynomial-vector step there is no matrix-target column; use the full active row panel for the left update and then apply the right update to its active columns. After the block chase, perform the following exact upper-Hessenberg zero-pattern check, including when all its stages were identities. For $i=1,\ldots,n$ in increasing order, if $a\le i\le b$, test $h_{ij}=0$ for $j=1,\ldots,i-2$ in increasing order; otherwise test $h_{ij}=0$ for $j=a,\ldots,\min(b,i-2)$ in increasing order. Skip every empty index range. On the first nonzero tested entry return bulge-chase-invariant-failure with the partial matrix and factors. These are precisely the below-first-subdiagonal positions whose row or column belongs to $[a,b]$. Enumerate only these ranges; do not scan all $n^2$ positions and filter them. The unchanged complementary positions retain the zero values established by initialization or the previous accepted check. Deflation writes affect only the first subdiagonal and do not change those positions. Use [[lem-two-sided-scaled-householder-similarity-error]] to store the proved two-sided coefficient $\alpha_{m_j}=a_{m_j}+b_{m_j}+a_{m_j}b_{m_j}$, with $a$ the target-overwrite coefficient or separate-block coefficient as actually used and $b$ the right separate-block coefficient. This gives $\|E_j\|_F\le\alpha_{m_j}\|\widehat H_{j-1}\|_F$ when its $m_ju<1$ and range hypotheses hold. Apply the same certificate to every Hessenberg-initialization similarity. If any step lacks that certificate, retain the residual diagnostic and set the backward-error-certificate status to inconclusive.
5. Inspect maximal intervals in increasing left endpoint. A size-one interval is completed. A complex interval of size at least two, or a real interval of size at least three, is active. For each real size-two interval determine its exact discriminant sign as below: a negative sign completes that interval, while zero or a positive sign leaves it active. Stop with Schur-computed when all intervals are completed. Use the supplied evaluator, or the finite integer recipe in [[lem-exact-rational-two-by-two-discriminant-sign]] when exact rational/dyadic encodings are available, for each real block's $\operatorname{discSign}$ as defined in [[def-exact-real-2x2-discriminant-sign-predicate]]. If no exact sign is available, return schur-type-undecided and do not claim Schur-computed. If any active interval remains and $k=N$, return budget-exhausted; in particular, with $N=0$ return Schur-computed only when the initialized matrix already has the target block structure. Return the partial matrix and factors on every failure or nonconvergence status.

For certificate bookkeeping, start before Hessenberg initialization with $\rho_0=\operatorname{upnormF}(A)$ and $C_0=0$. If the evaluator is absent or this call is unavailable, mark the backward-error certificate inconclusive. Process each local similarity update and each deflation-only write as a separate finite stage $j$. For a local similarity, take the actual coefficient $\alpha_j=a_{m_j}+b_{m_j}+a_{m_j}b_{m_j}$ from [[lem-two-sided-scaled-householder-similarity-error]] and compute $\bar\alpha_j=\operatorname{upadd}(\operatorname{upadd}(a_{m_j},b_{m_j}),\operatorname{upmul}(a_{m_j},b_{m_j}))\ge\alpha_j$; for an identity update put $\bar\alpha_j=0$. A recorded deflation entry stores its old value, while its additive matrix $D_j$ has entry equal to zero minus that old value at the written position. For a deflation-only stage use $P_j=I$, $E_j=0$, $\bar\alpha_j=0$, and obtain $\bar\beta_j\ge\|D_j\|_F$ by calling `upnormF` on the one-entry list containing the signed recorded value, whose Frobenius norm equals $\|D_j\|_F$; do not form or scan a dense matrix $D_j$; for a similarity stage set $\bar\beta_j=0$. With the outward evaluator compute

$$g_j=\operatorname{upadd}(\operatorname{upmul}(\bar\alpha_j,\rho_{j-1}),\bar\beta_j),\qquad \rho_j=\operatorname{upadd}(\rho_{j-1},g_j),\qquad C_j=\operatorname{upadd}(C_{j-1},g_j).$$

If any local coefficient certificate or evaluator call is unavailable, keep the residual diagnostic and mark the backward-error-certificate status `inconclusive`; this ancillary failure does not change the main algorithm status. Otherwise return $C_J$ as the accumulated backward-error upper bound and mark that status `certified`. The number of recurrence calls is finite: one initialization norm, a fixed number of scalar upper-bound calls per similarity stage, and one norm call per deflation-only stage.

Let $\widehat T$ be the final returned matrix. The output includes the product representation $Q$, residual matrix $R=Q^*AQ-\widehat T$ and its Frobenius norm as diagnostics, the exact orthogonality bound $0$ for that reflector product, the recorded deflation entries, and either the accumulated backward-error bound when all local certificates exist or certificate status inconclusive. Bound expressions and any claimed upper bounds are evaluated exactly or with rigorous outward allowances; uncorrected rounded residual norms are diagnostics only. A rounded dense matrix formed from $Q$ has its own orthogonality residual and is not asserted exactly unitary. The residual diagnostic does not itself give a forward eigenvalue bound. The procedure asserts no unconditional convergence of any shift schedule.

derivations.claim: Hessenberg reduction uses at most $\max(n-2,0)$ reflector steps. For $n\ge3$, forming one reflector costs $O(n)$ scalar operations, and applying its two-sided similarity to the remaining dense submatrix costs $O(n^2)$; summing over at most $n$ steps gives $O(n^3)$. Any full initialization zero-pattern checks also cost at most $O(n^2)$ per stage, hence at most $O(n^3)$ in total. For $n=1,2$, there are no such reflector stages and no below-subdiagonal entries.

For an active block of size $r\ge2$, a Francis sweep has at most $\max(r-2,0)+1$ initial/chase reflectors of length two or three. Each acts on a bounded number of rows and columns across at most $n$ entries. For a processed interval $[a,b]$ of length $r$, every matrix write has a row or column in that interval. Before the chase, initialization or the preceding accepted check has established that the complementary below-subdiagonal positions are zero. The prescribed post-block check enumerates only the positions touching this interval: at most $nr$ in its rows and $nr$ in its columns, plus the $n$ row-loop visits. It is therefore equivalent to the full Hessenberg check and costs $O(nr)$, since every active interval has $r\ge2$. The disjoint active lengths sum to at most $n$, so all these checks cost $O(n^2)$ per sweep, even if every polynomial vector is zero and all factors are identities. The explicit partition/deflation passes and direct shift-table lookups also fit within $O(n^2)$; for $n=1$ there is no active sweep. Thus a full sweep, including all non-controller status work, costs $O(n^2)$. The linear sweep budgets therefore give $O(n^3)$ matrix work for the two Schur calls. A range, breakdown, invariant, budget, missing-shift or unavailable-sign failure stops within these bounded loops and adds only its partial-output work; it cannot increase their worst-case count. The same bound covers materializing the recorded factor products: initialization contributes $O(n^3)$ and each bounded-support chase factor updates only a bounded number of dense-factor columns, at cost $O(n)$.

Each exact Schur-certificate matrix product, the transform $U^*CV$, and the final transform $UYV^*$ cost $O(n^3)$. The block substitution has at most $n^2$ block pairs; each pair sums at most $O(n)$ earlier blocks of bounded size and solves a system of dimension at most four, so all substitution work is $O(n^3)$.

Each sweep checks at most $O(n)$ active blocks, and initialization and final checks add at most $O(n)$ such calls. With $O(n)$ sweeps there are at most $O(n^2)$ sign/representation-controller calls. A bounded call executes at most $K$ instructions, giving $O(Kn^2)$ work; the fixed built-in exact polynomial tree and rational/dyadic recipe are constant-size special cases. In arbitrary-terminating mode their actual total work is precisely the additional $C_{\rm aux}$.

The backward-error accumulator starts with one outward Frobenius norm of the input, costing $O(n^2)$ by the declared entrywise evaluator model. Each similarity uses a fixed number of scalar upper-bound calls once its local coefficient is evaluated. The explicit real/complex coefficient formulas require $O(m)$ scalar operations on active dimension $m$: their dimension-dependent powers can be formed by repeated multiplication and a square root for a half-integer exponent. Thus the at most $n$ initialization coefficients cost $O(n^2)$ in total, while each length-two/three chase coefficient costs $O(1)$. There are $O(n^2)$ chase similarities over the linear number of sweeps. Each recorded one-entry deflation has Frobenius norm equal to the modulus of its signed stored value, evaluated from that one-entry list with $O(1)$ scalar work; at most $O(n)$ such writes occur per sweep, hence $O(n^2)$ in total. Each stage then makes a fixed number of recurrence calls. Unavailable coefficient/evaluator results only stop certificate bookkeeping. Consequently this entire ancillary accumulation costs $O(n^2)$ and fits inside the cubic matrix-work bound, including failure branches.

The reductions, sweeps, exact certificates, transforms, block sums and fixed-size solves contribute $O(n^3)$, and step 1.4 supplies the complete control contribution. Adding them gives $O(n^3+Kn^2)$ and the fixed-$K$ cubic consequence, or $O(n^3+C_{\rm aux})$ for the richer terminating route. No bound on integer bit length or bit-operation cost is used.

Let $F\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$, $n\ge1$, and $A\in F^{n\times n}$. The matrix $A$ is **Hurwitz** if, when its eigenvalues are considered over $\mathbb C$, every eigenvalue has strictly negative real part. For $Q,X\in F^{n\times n}$ with $Q=Q^*$, the **continuous Lyapunov equation** with coefficient $A$ and forcing $Q$ is

$$
AX+XA^*+Q=0.
$$

Here $^*$ is transpose for real matrices and conjugate transpose for complex matrices. The notations $Q\succeq0$ and $Q\succ0$ mean that $Q$ is non-negative or positive as a self-adjoint operator in the sense of [[def-non-negative-and-positive-operator]]: respectively $v^*Qv\ge0$ for all $v$, or $v^*Qv>0$ for every nonzero $v$.
citations.use_explanation: [[def-hurwitz-matrix-and-continuous-lyapunov-equation]]: [[def-hurwitz-matrix-and-continuous-lyapunov-equation]]: $A$ is Hurwitz when all its eigenvalues have negative real part, and the balance is $AX+XA^T+Q=0$.

citations.quote:
Let $A\in F^{n\times n}$ be Hurwitz and let $Q=Q^*\in F^{n\times n}$. Then the improper matrix integral

$$
X=\int_0^\infty e^{tA}Qe^{tA^*}\,dt
$$

converges and is the unique solution of $AX+XA^*+Q=0$. If $Q\succeq0$, then $X\succeq0$. If $Q\succ0$, then $X\succ0$. For $Q\succeq0$, $X\succ0$ if and only if there is no nonzero $v$ for which $e^{tA^*}v\in\ker Q^{1/2}$ for every $t\ge0$.
citations.use_explanation: [[thm-continuous-lyapunov-integral-and-positivity]]: [[thm-continuous-lyapunov-integral-and-positivity]]: For Hurwitz $A$, the Lyapunov equation has a unique solution, and the integral solution is positive definite under the stated conditions.

derivations.claim: The eigenvalues of $A$ are $-1$ and $-2$, so $A$ is Hurwitz by [F1]. Direct multiplication gives $BB^T=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&1\end{pmatrix}$ and $AX+XA^T=\begin{pmatrix}-1&-1\\-1&-1\end{pmatrix}=-BB^T$. Thus the displayed $X$ solves the balance.
For real $(u,v)$, $\begin{pmatrix}u&v\end{pmatrix}X\begin{pmatrix}u\\v\end{pmatrix}=\frac12(u+\frac23v)^2+\frac1{36}v^2$, which is positive unless $u=v=0$. Hence $X\succ0$.
Since $A$ is Hurwitz, [F2] gives uniqueness of the solution, so this positive matrix is the unique stable Lyapunov covariance-balance solution.

For $F\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$, $A\in F^{m\times m}$, $B\in F^{n\times n}$ with $m,n\ge1$, define the Sylvester operator $\mathcal S_{A,B}:F^{m\times n}\to F^{m\times n}$ by

$$\mathcal S_{A,B}(X)=AX+XB.$$

Equip $F^{m\times n}$ with the Frobenius norm of [[def-frobenius-matrix-norm]]. The column-vectorization isometry of [[lem-sylvester-vectorization-isometry-and-kronecker-identity]] identifies this norm with the Euclidean norm on $F^{mn}$. Define

$$\operatorname{sep}(A,-B):=\sigma_{\min}(\mathcal S_{A,B})=\min_{\|X\|_F=1}\|AX+XB\|_F.$$

Here $\sigma_{\min}$ denotes the smallest singular value of the finite-dimensional linear map under these inner products. The finite-dimensional singular value decomposition [[thm-singular-value-decomposition]] ensures this minimum is well-defined. The argument $-B$ is part of the conventional label: the operator being measured is $X\mapsto AX+XB$.
citations.use_explanation: [[def-sylvester-operator-and-separation-number]]: [[def-sylvester-operator-and-separation-number]]: $\mathcal S_{A,B}(X)=AX+XB$ and $\operatorname{sep}(A,-B)=\sigma_{\min}(\mathcal S_{A,B})$ in the Frobenius inner product.

Let $F\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$, $m,n\ge1$, $A\in F^{m\times m}$ and $B\in F^{n\times n}$. Spectra of real matrices are taken over $\mathbb C$. The map $\mathcal S_{A,B}$ of [[def-sylvester-operator-and-separation-number]] is invertible if and only if

$$
\sigma(A)\cap(-\sigma(B))=\varnothing.
$$

Equivalently, for every $C\in F^{m\times n}$, the equation $AX+XB=C$ has a unique solution if and only if this spectral condition holds. The same condition is equivalent to $\operatorname{sep}(A,-B)>0$.
citations.use_explanation: [[thm-sylvester-unique-solvability-spectral-separation]]: [[thm-sylvester-unique-solvability-spectral-separation]]: Unique solvability holds exactly when $\sigma(A)\cap(-\sigma(B))=\varnothing$.

Let $X$ be the unique solution of $AX+XB=C$, and let $\widehat X\in F^{m\times n}$ be any approximation. Define its equation residual by $R=C-(A\widehat X+\widehat X B)$. If $\operatorname{sep}(A,-B)>0$, then

$$
\|X-\widehat X\|_F\le\frac{\|R\|_F}{\operatorname{sep}(A,-B)}.
$$
citations.use_explanation: [[thm-sylvester-residual-to-forward-error-bound]]: [[thm-sylvester-residual-to-forward-error-bound]]: $\|X-\widehat X\|_F\le\|C-(A\widehat X+\widehat X B)\|_F/\operatorname{sep}(A,-B)$ when the solution is unique.

derivations.claim: The eigenvalue sums are $\varepsilon,1,1+\varepsilon,2$, all nonzero, so [F2] gives a unique solution. In the Frobenius-orthonormal matrix-unit basis, $\mathcal S_{A,B}(E_{ij})=(a_{ii}+b_{jj})E_{ij}$; its singular values are therefore the four absolute eigenvalue sums, and [F1] gives $\operatorname{sep}(A,-B)=\varepsilon$.
The $(i,j)$ equation is $(a_{ii}+b_{jj})x_{ij}=c_{ij}$. Since $C=E_{11}$, the only nonzero entry is $x_{11}=1/\varepsilon$, hence $X=\varepsilon^{-1}E_{11}$ and $\|X\|_F=1/\varepsilon=10^6$.

If the right-hand side is perturbed by $\delta E_{11}$, the solution changes by $\delta/\varepsilon E_{11}$, whose Frobenius norm is $|\delta|/\varepsilon$. This attains the separation factor in [F3], verifying the stated sensitivity exactly.

Let $A\in F^{n\times n}$ be Hurwitz, let $B\in F^{n\times r}$, and let $p_1,\ldots,p_k\in\mathbb C$ be a finite shift list. The target equation is $AX+XA^*+BB^*=0$. Inputs also include the shift list and exact linear-solve operations. For real $A,B$, nonreal shifts must occur in consecutive complex-conjugate pairs; the procedure may use complex arithmetic for these paired shifts.

Before starting matrix updates, validate the real-data shift pairing by scanning the shift list once: at a real shift advance the scan index by one; at a nonreal shift require the next list entry to equal its complex conjugate, then advance the scan index by two. A missing or unequal partner returns `unpaired-complex-shift`. For complex data no pairing restriction is imposed. This validation scan consumes pairs; the update loop below still processes every individual shift in order.

Initialize $R_0=B$, let $Z_0$ have zero columns, and set $X_0=0$. For $j=1,\ldots,k$:

1. If $\operatorname{Re}p_j\ge0$, return `invalid-shift`. If $A+p_jI$ is singular, return `singular-shift`.
2. Set $c_j=-2\operatorname{Re}p_j>0$ and solve
   $$
   V_j=(A+p_jI)^{-1}R_{j-1}.
   $$
3. Set
   $$
   Z_j=[Z_{j-1},\sqrt{c_j}V_j],\qquad X_j=Z_jZ_j^*=X_{j-1}+c_jV_jV_j^*,\qquad R_j=R_{j-1}+c_jV_j.
   $$

Return `completed` with the low-rank factor $Z_k$, approximation $X_k$, and residual factor $R_k$. A finite shift list may stop before convergence; this procedure does not select shifts or assert unconditional convergence.

Let $F\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$, $m,n\ge1$, $A\in F^{m\times m}$, $B\in F^{n\times n}$ and $C\in F^{m\times n}$. Inputs also include a pivot threshold $\tau\ge0$, Schur controls for each matrix, a fixed constant $c_0>0$, and finite sweep budgets $N_A\le c_0m$, $N_B\le c_0n$. The local transforms, certificate checks and block substitution use exact scalar arithmetic and comparisons. The delegated Schur calls retain their specified rounded arithmetic, admissible input representations, range conditions and statuses; their returned factors remain candidates until the exact checks below succeed.

The default real-block sign controller is the fixed exact real-arithmetic expression tree $s=(a-d)^2+4bc$, followed by its sign comparisons, for [[def-exact-real-2x2-discriminant-sign-predicate]]. This uses five exact arithmetic operations and at most two sign comparisons in the declared exact local arithmetic model. For rational/dyadic encoded stored values, [[lem-exact-rational-two-by-two-discriminant-sign]] gives the finite exact integer realization; a fixed-format decoder, when used, is included in the control cost. These exact controller operations are separate from the rounded Schur matrix updates. No bit-complexity bound for integer/rational arithmetic is claimed.

Choose either bounded-controller mode, the default, or arbitrary-terminating-controller mode. In bounded mode supply a nonnegative integer per-call budget $K$. Custom sign or decoding routines are finite instruction programs over exact scalar real/integer arithmetic, comparisons, register operations and branches; no opaque callback is a unit instruction. The interpreter charges one unit per executed instruction, including decoding, the built-in tree and any custom-result verification within the same per-call $K$ budget; it checks instruction/operation validity when encountered and returns undecided on exhaustion or invalid execution. An undecided sign is propagated as the Schur type-undecided status and then outer `schur-failure`. The fixed built-in sign tree or integer recipe has a fixed finite instruction count independent of matrix dimension. Any custom reported sign must agree with the built-in exact discriminant tree before acceptance. In arbitrary-terminating mode custom programs must terminate on every supplied input; record their total executed controller work as $C_{\rm aux}$. This richer mode retains finite termination but has the additional work in its cost bound. In the cubic-cost branch $K$ and representation-control instruction costs are fixed independently of matrix dimension. Programs are executed by instruction lookup without an up-front scan of unused code.

1. Run [[alg-finite-budget-francis-schur-reduction]] on $A$ and $B$ with their supplied controls and budgets. If either call does not return `Schur-computed`, return `schur-failure` with the underlying status.

2. Treat the returned factors as candidates and verify the exact certificates. In the complex branch check $U^*U=I$, $A=UTU^*$, and upper triangularity of $T$; in the real branch check $U^TU=I$, $A=UTU^T$, and the real block upper-triangular form of [[def-real-and-complex-schur-forms]]. Perform the corresponding checks for $B=VSV^*$. If any check fails, return `schur-certificate-failure`.

3. Set $D=U^*CV$. Use the column-vectorization and Kronecker convention of [[lem-sylvester-vectorization-isometry-and-kronecker-identity]]. Partition $T$ into diagonal blocks $T_{ii}$ and $S$ into diagonal blocks $S_{jj}$ as in the exact real or complex Schur form. Traverse $j$ from left to right and, for each $j$, traverse $i$ from bottom to top. Form

$$
F_{ij}=D_{ij}-\sum_{k>i}T_{ik}Y_{kj}-\sum_{\ell<j}Y_{i\ell}S_{\ell j}.
$$

The terms on the right have already been computed in this traversal order. Define $\Phi_{ij}(Z)=T_{ii}Z+ZS_{jj}$ and its matrix representation $M_{ij}=I_{s_j}\otimes T_{ii}+S_{jj}^T\otimes I_{r_i}$ on column-vectorized blocks, where $r_i,s_j\in\{1,2\}$ are the block sizes. Let $q=r_is_j\le4$ and compute $\delta(M_{ij})$ from [[lem-small-block-determinant-separation-lower-bound]]. If $\det(M_{ij})=0$, return `singular-pivot`; if $\det(M_{ij})\ne0$ and $\delta(M_{ij})\le\tau$, return `pivot-separation-failure` because the requested pivot bound is not certified. Otherwise use the cofactor adjugate formula of [[lem-adjugate-inverse-formula-over-a-field]] to set $\operatorname{vec}(Y_{ij})=\operatorname{adj}(M_{ij})\operatorname{vec}(F_{ij})/\det(M_{ij})$ and store $Y_{ij}$. The local dimension is at most four in the real block case and one in the complex triangular case.

4. After all blocks are solved, return `success` and $X=UYV^*$, together with the exact residual $C-(AX+XB)$. No computed Schur candidate is accepted as an exact factorization unless step 2 verifies its defining equalities.

Let $F$ be a field, $q\ge1$, and $M\in F^{q\times q}$. Let $\operatorname{adj}(M)$ be the adjugate defined by the cofactors of [[def-matrix-minors-cofactors-and-adjugate]]. Then

$$
M\operatorname{adj}(M)=\det(M)I_q.
$$

Consequently, when $\det(M)\ne0$, $M^{-1}=\operatorname{adj}(M)/\det(M)$; when $\det(M)=0$, $M$ is singular.

For admitted inputs of [[alg-finite-budget-francis-schur-reduction]], including its terminating sign and outward-bound evaluators when supplied, the procedure terminates with one of its defined main statuses after finite initialization and at most $N$ sweeps. Its separate backward-certificate flag is `certified` only when every required local/evaluator bound is available, and otherwise is `inconclusive`. A `Schur-computed` return has the verified real or complex block pattern; its recorded exact reflector product is unitary. This asserts neither an exact Schur factorization of the original matrix nor convergence of any shift schedule, a forward spectral bound, or exact unitarity of a rounded dense product.

Suppose [[alg-bartels-stewart-sylvester-equation]] returns `success` for $A,B,C$. Then its returned $X$ satisfies $AX+XB=C$. If $\sigma(A)\cap(-\sigma(B))=\varnothing$, this $X$ is the unique solution.

There are finitely many block pairs and finitely many terms in each substitution sum. Let $A\in F^{n\times n}$ be Hurwitz, let $B\in F^{n\times r}$, and let $p_1,\ldots,p_k\in\mathbb C$ be a finite shift list. The target equation is $AX+XA^*+BB^*=0$. Inputs also include the shift list and exact linear-solve operations. For real $A,B$, nonreal shifts must occur in consecutive complex-conjugate pairs; the procedure may use complex arithmetic for these paired shifts.

Before starting matrix updates, validate the real-data shift pairing by scanning the shift list once: at a real shift advance the scan index by one; at a nonreal shift require the next list entry to equal its complex conjugate, then advance the scan index by two. A missing or unequal partner returns `unpaired-complex-shift`. For complex data no pairing restriction is imposed. This validation scan consumes pairs; the update loop below still processes every individual shift in order.

Initialize $R_0=B$, let $Z_0$ have zero columns, and set $X_0=0$. For $j=1,\ldots,k$:

1. If $\operatorname{Re}p_j\ge0$, return `invalid-shift`. If $A+p_jI$ is singular, return `singular-shift`.
2. Set $c_j=-2\operatorname{Re}p_j>0$ and solve
   $$
   V_j=(A+p_jI)^{-1}R_{j-1}.
   $$
3. Set
   $$
   Z_j=[Z_{j-1},\sqrt{c_j}V_j],\qquad X_j=Z_jZ_j^*=X_{j-1}+c_jV_jV_j^*,\qquad R_j=R_{j-1}+c_jV_j.
   $$

Return `completed` with the low-rank factor $Z_k$, approximation $X_k$, and residual factor $R_k$. A finite shift list may stop before convergence; this procedure does not select shifts or assert unconditional convergence.
If $A$ is Hurwitz and $p\in\mathbb C$ has $\operatorname{Re}p<0$, then $A+pI$ is invertible over $\mathbb C$.

The update loop still visits both indices.

Each valid update has $c_j=-2\operatorname{Re}p_j>0$. By [F2] its exact linear system has a unique solution. Other shift checks return their declared status. A **field** is a set $F$ equipped with two binary operations $+$ (addition) and
$\cdot$ (multiplication) and two distinguished elements $0 \ne 1$ of $F$,
satisfying:

- **(A)** $(F, +)$ is an abelian group with identity $0$: addition is
  associative and commutative, $x + 0 = x$ for all $x$, and every $x$ has an
  additive inverse $-x$ with $x + (-x) = 0$.
- **(M)** Multiplication is associative and commutative **on all of $F$**, and
  $x \cdot 1 = x$ for every $x \in F$; moreover $(F \setminus \{0\}, \cdot)$ is an
  abelian group with identity $1$, so every $x \ne 0$ has a multiplicative inverse
  $x^{-1}$ with $x \cdot x^{-1} = 1$.
- **(D)** Multiplication distributes over addition: $x \cdot (y + z) = x\cdot y + x\cdot z$.

We write $x - y := x + (-y)$ and $x/y := x \cdot y^{-1}$ (for $y \ne 0$), and
abbreviate $x \cdot y$ as $xy$.

An **ordered field** is a field $F$ ([[def-field]]) together with a subset
$P \subseteq F$, the set of **positive** elements (the *positive cone*),
satisfying:

- **(O1) Trichotomy.** For each $x \in F$, exactly one of the following holds:
  $x \in P$, or $x = 0$, or $-x \in P$.
- **(O2) Closure.** If $x, y \in P$ then $x + y \in P$ and $x \cdot y \in P$.

We write $x > 0$ for $x \in P$ (read "$x$ is positive"), and define the order by

$$a < b \;:\Longleftrightarrow\; b - a \in P, \qquad a \le b \;:\Longleftrightarrow\; a < b \text{ or } a = b.$$

Thus $a > b$ means $b < a$, and $a \ge b$ means $b \le a$. An element $x$ with
$-x \in P$ (equivalently $x < 0$) is called **negative**.

Let $F$ be an ordered field ([[def-ordered-field]]). The **absolute value** of
$x \in F$ is

$$|x| \;:=\; \begin{cases} x & \text{if } x \ge 0, \\ -x & \text{if } x < 0. \end{cases}$$

$(i,j)$ refers to CSR row $i-1$ and column index $j-1$. This row/column order
is fixed before the procedure begins; vector component label $i$ refers to
coordinate $i-1$. The procedure performs no pivoting or reordering. All field
operations below are exact.

Let $P=\{(i,j):a_{ij}\ne0\}$. Scan each row once to check the canonical and
increasing-index conditions and to record whether its diagonal position occurs.
If the input fails either pattern condition, return `invalid-pattern`. If a row
has no diagonal position, return `missing-diagonal(i)` for the least such $i$.

Copy the value in each input slot to a work array $W$, and regard the unit
diagonal of $L$ as implicit. Process rows $i=1,\ldots,n$ in increasing order.
For each $k<i$ with $(i,k)\in P$, in increasing $k$ order, do the following:

1. If $W_{kk}=0$, return `zero-pivot(k)`.
2. Set $W_{ik}\gets W_{ik}/W_{kk}$; this value is the stored factor $L_{ik}$.
3. Let $R$ be the increasing list of one-based matrix column labels $j>k$

   increasing list represented by row $k$'s CSR segment. Set each pointer to

   their lists, compare their current indices. If they are equal, call their

   $$W_{ij}\gets W_{ij}-W_{ik}W_{kj}$$

   advance only its pointer once; if the current index in $C$ is smaller,
   advance only its pointer once, making no arithmetic update in either
   unequal-index branch. Stop when either pointer passes the end of its list.

`zero-pivot(i)`. Otherwise the upper row entries $U_{ij}$ are the current

Let $F$ be a field, and let $m,n,s\in\mathbb N$, where $\mathbb N$ includes
$0$. A **compressed sparse row (CSR) record** for an $m$ by $n$ matrix over
$F$ consists of integer arrays $r=(r_0,\ldots,r_m)$ and
$c=(c_0,\ldots,c_{s-1})$, and a value array $v=(v_0,\ldots,v_{s-1})\in F^s$,
satisfying

$$r_0=0,\qquad 0=r_0\le r_1\le\cdots\le r_m=s,\qquad 0\le c_t<n\quad(0\le t<s).$$

For each row $i<m$, its **stored entries** are the indices
$t$ with $r_i\le t<r_{i+1}$. The row is empty exactly when
$r_i=r_{i+1}$. Repeated column indices within one row and stored values
$v_t=0_F$ are permitted; each such entry remains a separate stored entry.

The represented matrix $A\in M_{m\times n}(F)$ is defined entrywise by

$$A_{ij}:=\sum_{r_i\le t<r_{i+1}}\mathbf 1_{c_t=j}v_t\qquad(0\le i<m,\ 0\le j<n),$$

where $\mathbf 1_{c_t=j}$ is $1_F$ when $c_t=j$ and $0_F$ otherwise, and an
empty sum is $0_F$. Repeated entries in column $j$ are therefore added. The
number $s$ is the **stored-entry count**; it is not in general the number of
nonzero entries of $A$.

A CSR record is **canonical** when no row repeats a column and no stored value
is zero. In that case every nonzero matrix entry is stored exactly once and
$s=\operatorname{nnz}(A)$, where $\operatorname{nnz}(A)$ denotes the number of
nonzero entries of $A$. If $m=0$, the endpoint conditions force $s=0$ and the
row-pointer array has its single entry $r_0=0$. If $n=0$, the column-index
condition forces $s=0$ as well.

derivations.claim: The input has finite arrays and $n$ is finite. Validation visits the $n$ row intervals and $s$ stored entries once; the factorization loops over at most $n$ rows, finitely many pattern entries, and finite row-list merges. Every division is preceded by a nonzero-pivot check, and [A1] makes each such division defined. Thus the procedure either returns one of its specified failure statuses or completes with `ok`.

If the procedure returns `ok`, each processed pivot is nonzero by its check, so the returned $U$ has nonzero diagonal. The definition sets $L$ to be unit lower triangular and retains only upper entries in $U$.

Initially the work values occupy exactly the input slots $P$. Each multiplier is written only at a strict-lower slot in $P_L$, and each update is performed only when both matching row positions are in $P$. No update allocates a new position. Induction over the finite row and pivot loops therefore gives stored patterns $P_L$ and $P_U$ for $L$ and $U$, respectively.

The forward recurrence in [F3] applied to unit-lower $L$ and the backward recurrence in [F4] applied to $U$ are well-defined because $L_{ii}=1$ and every $U_{ii}\ne0$. By [F5] and [F6] they produce the unique successive triangular-solve outputs specified by the algorithm.

The sets $P_L$ and $P_U$ are disjoint and partition $P$: every $(i,j)\in P$ has exactly one of $i>j$ or $i\le j$. Hence $\ell+q=|P|=s$. Since the unit diagonal of $L$ is implicit, this is exactly the factor numeric-slot count.

On success, the outer lower-pattern loop processes every one of the $\ell$ positions once and performs one division there. For a fixed $(i,k)\in P_L$, the update loop visits exactly the indices in $R_{ik}\cap C_k$; each visit performs one multiplication and one subtraction. Summing these counts gives exactly $\ell$ divisions and $I$ multiplications and subtractions.

Both lists in each intersection are strictly increasing. A two-pointer merge advances at least one pointer at every comparison and stops when one list ends, so it makes at most the sum of the two list lengths, $|R_{ik}|+|C_k|$, comparisons. Summing over $P_L$ gives the bound $J$; validation visits each row interval and stored entry once.

The forward recurrence in [F3] performs one multiplication and subtraction for each stored strict-lower slot, hence $\ell$ of each and no diagonal divisions. The backward recurrence in [F4] performs one multiplication and subtraction for each stored strict-upper slot, hence $u$ of each, and one division for each of its $n$ rows. Since $\ell+u=\ell+q-n=s-n$, the stated application counts follow.
